_comment: Public one-sentence descriptions of the designs the checker rejects (site/build.py, "What does not count"), keyed by the stem of the file in tests/<task>/negative/ (`negatives`) or tests/<task>/attacks/ (`attacks`). Every negative and attack of tests/expected.json that the checker rejects needs one; the stage comes from tests/expected.json. The internal notes there are never shown.

negatives.arith_and: The right function, written with run-time `+` and `-`, which this task bans.
negatives.extra_in: A hidden extra input port: the statement allows exactly the task's ports.
negatives.or_gate: The wrong function: OR instead of AND.
negatives.reads_x: Reads a net that nothing drives, so its value is unknown (`x`).
negatives.wide_out: The output is N + 1 bits wide instead of N.

attacks.array_sum: Sums an unpacked array with the `.sum()` method: run-time addition in disguise.
attacks.casex_item: A `case` item with an `x` digit: ls-sv computes `a & b`, while Yosys treats the item as a match and drives an unknown value at 0 GE.
attacks.fn_uninit: A function reads a local variable before assigning it: unknown in SystemVerilog, a fixed value in Yosys, and a construct ls-sv cannot run.
attacks.for_counter_skip: A `for` loop that skips an iteration by incrementing its own counter: simulation and synthesis disagree on the result.
attacks.for_counter_write: A `for` loop whose body overwrites its own counter: Yosys ignores the write, while a simulator can loop forever.
attacks.latch_never: An `always_latch` that is never enabled: unknown in simulation, while Yosys resolves the latch to a constant.
attacks.latch_star: The same never-enabled latch, written with `always @*`.
attacks.oob_rare: An out-of-range read that changes the netlist's output on a single input pair, too rare for any sampling to find.
attacks.oob_select: An index that always reads past the end of a 4-bit vector: an unknown value that ls-sv and Yosys resolve differently.
attacks.param_divzero: A constant `1 / 0` used as a `case` item: an unknown value without an `x` literal, matched by Yosys and never by ls-sv.
attacks.priority_nomatch: A `priority case` that never matches, which lets Yosys drive anything (0 GE).
attacks.rare_mid: An out-of-range read that changes the output on about one input in 512: sampling finds it only with the full vector set.
attacks.undriven_mux: A multiplexer steered by a signal that nothing drives: ls-sv and Yosys pick different branches.
attacks.undriven_offpoint: The same undriven multiplexer, driven at the scoring width N = 16 only: at every other width ls-sv and Yosys pick different branches.
attacks.unique0_nomatch: A harmless `unique0 case` that never matches, refused like every `unique`, `unique0` and `priority` qualifier because they let synthesis read a `case` differently from simulation.
attacks.unique_first_const: A harmless-looking `unique case (1'b1)` whose first item is the constant 1, so two items can match at once.
attacks.unique_nomatch: A `unique case` that never matches, which lets Yosys drive anything (0 GE).
attacks.unique_overlap: A `unique case` with overlapping items, where Yosys ORs the arms of the items that both match.
attacks.unique_rare: The same overlap confined to one input pattern in 2^24.
attacks.z_rare: A `case` item with `z` digits that Yosys ignores, so the netlist differs on one input in 2^28.
attacks.zconst_param: `x` and `z` bits hidden in local parameters built by concatenation, used as `case` items.
attacks.zeq_pair_if: Comparisons against constants with `z` digits: unknown in ls-sv, always true in Yosys.
attacks.zpair_or: Two complementary `case` items with `z` digits: neither matches in ls-sv, together they match every input in Yosys.
